title: Stability and Generalization in Looped Transformers
abstract: arXiv:2604.15259v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Looped transformers promise test-time compute scaling by spending more iterations on harder problems, but it remains unclear which architectural choices let them extrapolate to harder problems at test time rather than memorize training-specific solutions. We introduce a fixed-point based framework for analyzing looped architectures along three axes of stability -- local attractivity, input-dependence, and geometry -- and use it to characterize when fixed-point iteration yields meaningful predictions. Theoretically, we prove that looped networks without recall have countable fixed points and cannot achieve strong input-dependence at any spectral regime, while recall with outer normalization reliably produces a regime in which fixed points are simultaneously locally-attractive, locally smooth in the input, and supported by stable backpropagation. translated_title: 循环Transformer中的稳定性与泛化
translated_abstract: 循环Transformer通过在更难的问题上投入更多迭代次数，有望实现测试时的计算扩展，但目前仍不清楚哪些架构选择能让它们在测试时外推到更难的问题，而非死记硬背训练中特定的解法。我们提出了一个基于不动点的分析框架，从局部吸引性、输入依赖性和几何结构这三个稳定性维度来分析循环架构，并用它刻画不动点迭代何时能产生有意义的预测。在理论上，我们证明了不带召回机制的循环网络具有可数个不动点，且在任何谱范围内都无法实现强输入依赖性；而带外部归一化的召回机制则能可靠地产生一种状态，使得不动点同时具备局部吸引性、对输入的局部平滑性，并获得稳定反向传播的支持。在实证方面，我们在国际象棋、数独和前缀和任务上训练了小型循环Transformer（摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出基于不动点的三维度稳定性分析框架，证明带外部归一化召回机制的循环Transformer能同时实现不动点的局部吸引性、输入平滑性与稳定的反向传播，从而在测试时对更难的问题实现外推而非记忆。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a fixed-point framework analyzing stability along local attractivity, input-dependence, and geometry, proving that recall with outer normalization enables looped transformers to achieve locally attractive, input-smooth fixed points with stable backpropagation, thereby extrapolating to harder problems at test time rather than memorizing.
